fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents present a credible QA-to-platform transition rather than manufacture senior infrastructure experience. Personal Terraform/AWS work, limited Kubernetes access and the pending CKA are clearly qualified. However, this remains a substantial stretch for an independent contractor expected to lead production cloud architecture: Terragrunt, mTLS, manufacturer integration and production cloud ownership are not established. These gaps need not all be itemised, but the application does not offer a convincing bridge to the engagement's level of independence.

artefacts: The approximation mark in '~25 developers' is lost in the PDF, leaving '( 25 developers)'.
issues: Professional project bullets substantially duplicate the experience section, increasing length without much additional evidence.
The selected projects are not consistently date-ordered: the 2022 project precedes the 2023 dashboard project.
The second page is only 34.1% filled while the first page is comparatively dense.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in sensible order and uses standard headings.
Coverage includes semantic equivalents: TLS, cert-manager, monitoring tools and a VPS, rather than all exact keyword strings.
The current job title and most professional evidence remain QA/test-infrastructure focused.
Strong Terraform/Terragrunt and production cloud architecture requirements are not met by the explicitly personal/basic experience.
Java test automation should not be counted as a JVM backend background.

issues: The opening's 'This has given me ... GitOps' blurs personal homelab work with professional experience.
The third paragraph is overloaded with tools, qualifications and mentoring evidence.
Personal Terraform and namespace-level Kubernetes limitations are explained twice, making the conclusion repetitive and defensive.
Company specificity is limited to the new fleet/cloud connection; no additional company research is meaningfully used.
It largely retells the CV rather than explaining how this transitional background could meet an independently led production engagement.
strengths: Correct company and contractor role, with no stale earlier-application framing.
Strong, supported pipeline performance and cost metrics.
Personal projects, AWS basics and pending certification are honestly qualified.
The train-to-cloud project is explicitly connected to the candidate's automation and monitoring background.
Professional tone and a one-page presentation.

statements_in_outputs: I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role.
I would bring a practical automation background and a clear understanding of those boundaries to the engagement.

spacing_issues: The CV's first page is dense, whereas page two contains only roughly one-third of a page of content.
Repeated professional-project material contributes to the unbalanced pagination.
The cover letter's long third paragraph creates a visually heavy block.
issues: The CV's 10-point body and 9-point dates are readable but relatively small.
There is no continuation heading at the top of CV page two, which starts directly with a project.
The PDF visibly renders '( 25 developers)' with an awkward space where the approximation mark should be.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'I also configured ... I also provisioned ... I have also used ... I also wrote' is repetitive; vary or combine these constructions.

'I recognise that my Terraform experience is currently personal-project based and that my Kubernetes work has been at namespace and Helm-chart level' repeats qualifications already given immediately beforehand.
'Personal hands-on experience ... complements professional platform-adjacent work' is accurate but somewhat abstract and jargon-heavy.

notes_facts_used: CKA preparation, January 2027 booking and explicit not-yet-certified status.
AWS EC2/S3 basics confined to personal learning.
Namespace-level Kubernetes access and Helm-chart work rather than cluster administration.
The platform team operates the professional Kubernetes cluster, explicitly stated in the letter.
Internal CI documentation used for onboarding.
notes_facts_ignored: Observed two incident calls without having production on-call experience.
Explicit preference for a junior/mid DevOps or platform role and willingness to accept a junior title; the outputs convey transition but not the target level.

evaluation.summary: The outputs are mostly well-grounded and make good use of the candidate's pipeline metrics, homelab, documentation and mentoring experience. They correctly distinguish personal cloud/Terraform learning, namespace-level Kubernetes work and a pending CKA from production ownership or obtained certification. The principal weakness is the large gap between this transitional profile and a contractor expected to lead cloud architecture, strong Terraform/Terragrunt and secure train integration. The letter is repetitive and briefly misattributes GitOps to professional work, while duplicated CV content produces an unnecessarily unbalanced two-page layout.
